title: LangChain Middleware: Hooks for Agent State, Tools and Guardrails
summary: Dmitri Iourovitski explains LangChain middleware: hooks that run before and after the agent and the model.
learn: LangChain middleware has four hooks: before agent, before model, after model and after agent.
Before agent is the place to set up heavy resources, such as the shell tool environment, so the agent does not have to create one mid-run.
Before model is where dynamic state, such as the to-do list, goes into the system prompt, and where tools can be selected with the built-in tool selector middleware.
After model, middleware can run safety checks, limit tool calls and cache web service calls.
Iourovitski says agents often claim they are done when they are not, and an after agent hook can jump back to the model.
Modifying messages can break the prompt cache, and Iourovitski says removing parts of tool calls makes Anthropic return a 500 error.
